module_title: Software Sub-Categories - Utilities, Device Drivers, and App Types
introduction: This intermediate tier focuses on the sub-categories of software. Aspirants frequently make mistakes when asked to categorize 'Utility Software' and 'Device Drivers'. We will also distinguish between general and specific-purpose applications.

core_concepts.title: Utility Software
core_concepts.description:
This is a sub-type of **System Software** designed to maintain, protect, and optimize the computer. 
Examples: Antivirus, Disk Defragmenter, Backup utilities, and File Compression tools (WinRAR).

core_concepts.title: Device Drivers
core_concepts.description: This is also a sub-type of **System Software**. It is a specialized program that teaches the Operating System how to communicate with new external hardware (like a new printer, webcam, or graphics card).

core_concepts.title: General Purpose Application Software
core_concepts.description:
Ready-made applications designed to meet the common needs of the general public. 
Examples: MS Office suite, Web browsers, Adobe Photoshop.

core_concepts.title: Specific Purpose (Customized) Application Software
core_concepts.description:
Tailor-made software developed strictly for a specific organization or a unique task. 
Examples: Railway Reservation System (IRCTC), a Bank's Core Banking software, or a School's Fee Management system.

important_entities.name: Antivirus
important_entities.significance: It removes malware and ensures the smooth functioning of the system, acting as a maintenance tool rather than a user-task tool.

important_entities.name: Background vs. Foreground
important_entities.significance: System software (like the OS and Utilities) constantly runs in the 'background' to keep the PC alive. Application software runs in the 'foreground' when you actively open it.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because users manually install Antivirus programs (like Norton or QuickHeal), candidates incorrectly classify them as Application Software. This is a fatal mistake. Antivirus is 'Utility Software', which legally falls under the umbrella of System Software.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Just like a car needs a driver to operate, the Operating System needs a 'Device Driver' software to operate newly attached hardware.

exam_strategy_tips: A frequent banking/SSC question asks: 'Which software acts as a translator between the OS and a peripheral device?' The exact answer is 'Device Driver'.
